_doc: Owned by AI-C. Loading / idle tips for B. Shape: {tips:[{text(<=90 chars), kind: tool|hint|lore}]}. Pick one at random per loading screen; 'tool' tips are hints about the five bench tools.

tips.text: The Magnifier reads initials and station stamps.
The Lamp shows true colour and what a thing is made of.
Hold the Ear to anything that rattles, ticks or hums.
The Nose remembers: lavender, pipe smoke, wet wool.
The Brush reveals wear. Well-loved things look it.
Claimants rarely lie about the colour. Imposters get one detail wrong.
Shy owners answer better if you do not rush them.
Grumpy does not mean guilty. It usually means cold.
Hurried owners give short answers. Ask the sharp question first.
Worried owners remember the little things. Let them talk.
Check what an owner said against the bench, every time.
Your shelf never fills up. Keep everything.
A porter saves your legs. Worth the first tokens.
Refusing an imposter is a kindness to the real owner.
Items you cannot place now may suit someone at the next stop.
The Zero Line has no last stop. It has only the next one.
Everyone on board lost something they could not let go of.
The brass clock at the counter runs a little slow, on purpose.
Conductors never sit. They say it is for the view.
Some seats are always warm, whoever was last in them.
Under the seats is where the train keeps its secrets.
The tunnel is long, but never as long as it feels.
Rain on the roof means the dining car is at its best.
The night train smells of pipe smoke and oranges.
Nobody remembers boarding. Everybody remembers why.
Platform Zero is on no map, and on every ticket.
Lost mittens turn up in pairs, eventually.
The lamp over the bench has never once gone out.
Some passengers have ridden for years. They like the company.
A ticket stub can be the heaviest thing on the train.
The vendor's cart squeaks in B flat.
Snow muffles everything, even the whistle.
Desert nights are the quietest on the whole line.
Tea in the dining car is always just the right temperature.
Forget something tonight, and the Zero Line will keep it for you.
Night Case unsolved? It will wait for you until tomorrow.
Reputation only goes up. Take your time.
Tokens spent on lamp oil pay for themselves.
Glowing spots are worth a look. Something small is usually hiding.
Every lost thing has an owner somewhere. That is the whole job.
